note: Russia says it is ready in principle to resume peace talks, and the US president says the war is closer than ever to ending. The BBC's Russia editor and the Kremlin's own doubts about Ukrainian and European proposals suggest Moscow does not feel pressed to end the war.

note: Iran's IRGC says it hit four vessels in the northern Gulf and that three more struck mines near the Strait of Hormuz, while attacks in Saudi Arabia add to supply fears. Prices rose to their highest in five months.

note: A person briefed on war planning tells NPR that the US and Israel are preparing options for an attack after the US midterm elections, and Iran says it is prepared. Other outlets report similar plans, which fits the diplomatic drawdowns across the Gulf.

title: North Korea says border loudspeaker broadcasts into the South will resume within days
note: The North Korean leader's sister says anti-Seoul propaganda broadcasts will be ready within days and warns of new counter measures at the border. The move undercuts South Korea's president's efforts to ease inter-Korean hostility.
limitations: The item reports a statement of intent and does not confirm that broadcasts have started. Drafted by an automated daily job from the linked report; not yet reviewed.

title: TSMC seeks factory-equipment alternatives to avoid China's rare earth grip
note: Sources say the chipmaker is looking for equipment that does not depend on rare-earth magnets, which power motors in automated factories. It shows how export controls on critical minerals push firms to rework supply chains.
limitations: Relies on unnamed sources, and the item does not quantify any supply shortfall. Drafted by an automated daily job from the linked report; not yet reviewed.

title: Germany arrests Ukrainian national suspected of spying for Russia
